newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's AvtoZAZ raises charter capital 60 times.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's AvtoZAZ raises charter capital 60 times.

text.p: Ukraine's AvtoZAZ car maker, which is due to produce cars with South Korean Daewoo Group and General Motors of the U.S., will increase its charter capital by over 60 times, AvtoZAZ said on Thursday.
AvtoZAZ said in a statement that shareholders had voted this week to raise the capital to 581.8 million hryvnias from 9.5 million hryvnias ($5.3 million).
The AvtoZAZ statement also said shareholders had voted to issue 2,327,364 shares worth 0.25 hryvnia each, to be divided equally between shareholders.
Daewoo won a tender to produce cars and has since agreed to form a joint venture with GM.

Senior Daewoo officials have said the group was ready to invest about $1 billion, while privatisation officials say Kiev would give the strategic investor between 26 and 51 percent of shares in AvtoZAZ.
The state currently has an 86.5 percent stake.

Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said last week that AvtoZAZ, located in the industrial city of Zaporizhya located 600 km (330 miles) south-east of the capital Kiev, would produce 220,000-255,000 cars annually in four years time.
Lazarenko said AvtoZAZ would produce 150,000 Daewoo cars, 35,000 of GM's Opel Vectras and 70,000 small Ukrainian city models, the Dana and Tavris, which would be modernised.
